note: These propositions are self-contained study factoids distilled from the Dense-X paper for retrieval-granularity experiments.

propositions.text: Dense-X Retrieval studies which text granularity should be used as the retrieval unit in dense retrieval systems.
A proposition is an atomic expression in text that is intended to carry one self-contained meaning.
Dense retrievers can retrieve passages that contain both useful evidence and distracting irrelevant content.
The paper argues that retrieval granularity is an overlooked design choice in retrieval-augmented question answering.
A sentence can contain multiple propositions, so sentence-level retrieval can still mix several facts into one index object.
A proposition-level index aims to retrieve compact evidence that is easier for a downstream answer generator to use.
FactoidWiki is a Wikipedia-derived dataset used to compare retrieval units such as passages, sentences, and propositions.
The Dense-X experiments evaluate retrieval granularity with open-domain question answering datasets and dense retrieval models.
Fine-grained retrieval can improve passage recall because several proposition hits may point back to the same relevant source passage.
The practical lesson of Dense-X is that chunking should be treated as an experimental retrieval-design choice, not as a fixed preprocessing step.
